sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Orthotrichum anomalum is a saxicolous moss that forms tiny cushions about 0.5 cm tall, especially on limestone and other mineral surfaces. It has been recorded from sea level to about 3,000 m.

sections.title: Leaves and capsules
sections.text: The leaves are about 2–3.8 mm long. The exserted capsules are about 1.8–2.4 mm long and usually have 16 ribs alternating between long and short.

sections.title: Reproduction
sections.text: Like other mosses, it reproduces by spores in a capsule; it has no flowers or fruits in the sense of flowering plants.
